RoboSystems 1.12.0 is the release where a filing becomes a file the platform
publishes, and a section of it something an MCP client can read whole. It
closes the 1.11 series (99 pull requests since v1.11.0) with the SEC pipeline
rebuilt on xbrlkit, every processed filing published to the public CDN as a
holon, a Tavi model and the document as filed, the `disclosures` /
`information-block` pair over that file and over a tenant's live report, the
first bank feed and the native-accounting cutover it needed, the AI Operators
moved onto the worker with prompt caching and a credit ceiling, and a run of
correctness fixes across the statements, the ledger's origin tracking and the
graph lifecycle.

## A whole filing is a file

- **The SEC adapter reads through xbrlkit** (#1352, #1353, #1354). The filing
  text layer (the iXBRL disclosure parser, the Item extractor, the table
  converter), the EDGAR, EFTS and Arelle clients, and the graph projection now
  come from the public `xbrlkit` package: the processor loads a filing, hands
  the model to `xbrlkit.parse`, and projects it with `xbrlkit.serialize.lpg` —
  the same ids, columns and rows `xbrlkit build` writes into a single-filing
  `.lbug` — and the graph schema's XBRL tables are declared from
  `xbrlkit.schema`. The processor went from 2,195 lines to 775. Arelle's
  per-process schema recheck — hundreds of conditional requests per filing,
  the thing that throttled corpus runs — is gone: a large 10-K on a warm cache
  went from 34 s and four hosts contacted to 0.7 s and none. `arelle-release`
  is no longer pinned here; it resolves through xbrlkit.
- **Every processed filing is published** (#1360, 1.11.16). A public folder per
  filing on the data CDN, `{year}/{cik}/{accession}/`, holds the JSON-LD holon,
  the Project Tavi compiled model with its gaps sidecar, the primary document
  as filed and a manifest; a catalog asset folds them into
  `companies/{ticker}.json` per filer and `companies/index.json`, rewritten
  whole. Both projections come from xbrlkit's emitters over the model the
  processor already holds — no graph read, no second parse. The index now says
  which filers have a filing a page can render (`renderable`,
  `latest_renderable`, #1387), carried forward run to run so the corpus
  reprocess can be watched through it. Filed documents and text fragments are
  served with `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`; the holon, the Tavi and the catalog are
  not. `SEC_FILING_ARTIFACTS_ENABLED`, default on.
- **`disclosures` and `information-block`** (#1386) — the two shaped tools
  `xbrlkit serve` runs over a loaded filing, now view operations under
  `/extensions/roboledger/{graph_id}/operations/` and MCP tools on `sec` and on
  tenant graphs. `disclosures` is the map: one row per disclosure family with
  block, fact and text-block counts, or one family's blocks with their ids.
  `information-block` is one section read whole: rows in presentation order,
  the same rows broken out by the section's own axes, every total's
  calculation children with a footing check, the section's text blocks —
  budgeted, not counted. On `sec` the report is the published holon, read
  in-cluster; on a tenant it is the ledger's live report through the bundle
  the exports already build. The graph is in neither path: a whole-report walk
  of the corpus graph was measured at 30–60 s of replica IO per filing. A
  filing processed before the artifacts existed answers 404 "not published
  yet" until the repository is reprocessed. The block rules stay in the xbrlkit
  library, imported by the API process. xbrlkit 0.15.0, which the processor now
  writes holons through, reads Calculations 1.1 as the calculation linkbase and
  carries `xbrldt:targetRole`, so a reprocessed filing foots and breaks out by
  dimension where the earlier holons could not.
- **The text index is complete** (#1348, #1352, #1357, #1359). Multi-page notes
  were cut after one continuation — a large 10-K yielded 110K characters of
  narrative and now yields 343K, one note going from 570 characters to
  130,272; long sections are indexed in parts instead of truncated at 50,000
  characters; a text block tagged more than once is one section; `ix:exclude`
  page headers are dropped; a ticker-less filer indexes under its CIK rather
  than the string `<NA>`. Existing documents keep the truncated form until the
  index is rebuilt (below). `examples/sec_corpus_check` audits a loaded corpus
  against the parsers (#1358).
- **The views keep the most precise fact** (#1348). `financial-statement-
  analysis` and `build-fact-grid` collapsed duplicates by keeping whichever row
  the engine returned first, so a figure reported on the statement face and
  again, rounded, in a note flipped between identical calls. Both now keep the
  most precise fact per period.
- **The SEC dump is a Hugging Face dataset** (#1302): a manual Dagster job
  copies the shared-repository snapshot to the Hub on the Hub's own compute,
  and `just sec-dump` pulls, verifies and decompresses it so a checkout serves
  the full corpus with no pipeline run.
- **The holon viewer is the xbrlkit viewer at `xbrlkit.com`** (#1370, #1372);
  `holon.robosystems.ai` stays as an alias. The API allows
  `MCP-Protocol-Version` through CORS preflight so a browser MCP client can
  speak Streamable HTTP (#1346).

## Native accounting and the Mercury bank feed

- **The cutover** (#1378, 1.11.19). A provider-compatibility guard: a bank
  feed beside a live QuickBooks connection, a bank feed on a graph with no
  chart of accounts, or QuickBooks over natively kept books each answer 409
  with a stable code. A `sever` disposition on `deleteConnection` cuts a
  QuickBooks tenant over to native books while keeping the chart QuickBooks
  created: the elements become native, `write_policy` drops to `native`, and a
  later re-authorization mints a fresh connection the guard then refuses. A
  plain disconnect now also resets `write_policy` to `native`.
  `initialize-chart-of-accounts` gives a fresh company a chart from a shipped
  template — `saas`, `services` or `product` — with its rs-gaap mapping
  created in the same operation; `chartTemplates` on the ledger GraphQL query
  lists them. The templates are data under `frameworks/chart-templates/`
  (#1379): a chart per template plus one mapping file per framework, never
  seeded into the library.
- **Mercury, the first bank feed** (#1381, 1.11.20). The bank as a first-class
  source: every posted Mercury transaction is captured into the ledger inbox
  with a Tier-0 account suggestion attached; the feed authors no chart, no
  elements and no GL rows. One Dagster asset per sync, internal transfers
  paired into one event, one chart account linked or created per bank account
  through the Taxonomy Block envelope, and a disconnect that runs the
  partnership's deletion protocol. Off by default: `CONNECTION_MERCURY_ENABLED`
  needs Mercury's partner OAuth client, and the production client sits behind
  Mercury's compliance review.
- **Classify, then commit** (#1382, #1385). `captured → classified` records
  the account choice — an element, a split, or the suggestion as-is — and
  validates it against the chart; the commit builds the balanced entry and
  posts it as a draft that close posts, through the same journal handler every
  other event uses. An unclassified commit falls back to the tenant's
  deterministic rules and is refused when none matches. The MCP instructions
  gain an INBOX / BANK FEED block on graphs that expose the write tools. A
  placeholder posting date from the sandbox no longer opens the books at year
  1 (#1383); a mapped chart of accounts stays editable (#1384).
- **Retire an account** (#1380). `is_active=false` on an
  `update-taxonomy-block` element patch retires a chart account, and a new
  posting to it is refused with the account named and the way back. QuickBooks
  replays of already-posted history pass through.

## Reports and serialization

- **Tavi is a fourth download flavor** (#1361) for a published RoboLedger
  report, beside the JSON-LD, the holon and the XBRL 2.1 zip — the same
  standards form the SEC pipeline publishes per filing, so
  `@robosystems/report-components` renders both through one adapter. The
  emitter is xbrlkit's, over a new bundle-to-model bridge
  (`operations/serialization/model.py`), so a filing and a ledger report go
  through one implementation.
- **The holon too** (#1373, #1375). The platform's own holon partition seeded
  the scene from facts alone, so every element reached only by an arc — an
  empty statement line, an abstract header — rendered without a label: 56 of
  the SaaS demo's 98 elements. The holon now comes from xbrlkit's writer
  through the same bridge, carrying the platform's structure and fact-set ids
  so the flat JSON-LD and the holon of one report name the same things. The
  bridge also carries a block's type and an element's standard label into the
  model (#1386).
- **Report facts persist at cents** (#1362). Subtotals summed in float were
  stored with tails (`57985.020000000004`) and every published flavor printed
  them faithfully; the one choke point publication and canonical stamping
  both write through now rounds to cents. Existing reports keep their tails
  until regenerated.
- **Statements stop rendering numbers that looked authoritative and were not**
  (#1296): the comparative column of every live cash flow statement was the
  delta basis of the indirect method, not a statement, and rendered footed and
  wrong; `limit` defaults to the whole statement instead of 50 rows;
  `equity_statement` leaves the MCP financial-statement tools.
- **Validation means what it says** (#1303, #1304, #1306). The live statement
  ran no validation at all; now every rendered column is checked and the
  result rides on `live-financial-statement`. A block type with no rules
  reports `inconclusive`, not a green pass. Subtotals foot by calculation
  weight, so interest expense under nonoperating income stops reporting a
  difference the calc DAG got right. A zero credit balance renders as `$0.00`,
  not `-$0.00`.

## AI Operators

The console operator ran synchronously inside the API process and spent its
step budget on orientation. Across #1287–#1291, #1294, #1295, #1307 and #1308:

- **Every run executes on the background worker.**
  `POST /v1/graphs/{graph_id}/operator[/{operator_type}]` gates the request —
  lifecycle, limits, role, credits, with a 403 or 402 on the request itself —
  enqueues it, and answers 202 with the operation's links; `?mode=sync` waits
  up to 50 s and answers 200 when the result lands in time.
  `GET /v1/operations/{id}/status` reports `queue_position` and `queue_depth`,
  and the worker scales on real backlog. A new `awaiting_input` state and
  `POST /v1/operations/{id}/resume` give a human-gated run a way to pause
  before an irreversible step; no shipped task pauses yet.
- **Prompt caching, metered.** The system prefix — tool definitions, the whole
  graph schema, the example queries — is cached and read at a tenth of the
  input rate, and the meter reads all four Bedrock token counts so caching
  cannot leave input unbilled (#1288). A `standard` question's input bill fell
  by roughly two-thirds.
- **A wider read surface and a per-question ceiling.** Thirty-four read-only
  tools, from eight, with statement, balance and period questions routed to
  the curated tools before raw Cypher; `max_credits` caps a question; a
  corrected retry after a failed tool call is not charged against the step
  budget; the wrap-up turn is guaranteed to be text. A cancelled run stops
  calling the model, including one cancelled while it waited in the queue.
- **Memory in front of the question.** The memories most similar to the
  question are prefetched into the user turn, so the operator reads what
  earlier sessions stored at no tool-turn cost.
- **The operator is `analyst`**; `cypher` remains as an alias, so
  `POST …/operator/cypher` keeps working. The default Bedrock model is Claude
  Sonnet 5, with Sonnet 4.6 as the fallback.
- The orchestrator's never-enabled response cache is removed (#1312), and the
  credit pre-flight on a shared repository reads the plan correctly (#1285).

## The MCP surface

- **A tool result is context the model pays for on every later turn.** Two
  measurements from the Filing Ladder benchmark drove three changes:
  `search-documents` hits drop the per-section element list nobody used to
  choose a hit and hoist shared filing fields to the root; `get-document-
  section` pages with `offset` and `length` the way xbrlkit's `read_text`
  does (#1376); `financial-statement-analysis` answers with the columns a
  filing presents — annual by default on an annual form, two balance-sheet
  and three flow-statement periods, `periods_omitted` when it cut — and rows
  drop the redundant `name` (#1377). A large 10-K's income statement went from
  50,043 characters to 18,531.
- **The authored tool descriptions survive** (#1301). The handler had been
  overwriting `read-graph-cypher` and `get-graph-schema` with a one-line scope
  on every graph; the guidance is back, and the SEC manifest's six Cypher rules
  ride on the description, the one surface every client reads.
- The tool manager splits read from write, so read-only surfaces get every
  pure read while the OLTP-backed reads stay off shared repositories (#1290).

## Ledger integrity

- **Journal entries on their own terms** (#1355). Everything a period close
  posted was invisible: the list surfaces walk transactions, and
  schedule-derived entries have none. A `journalEntries` GraphQL field reads
  entries directly, with `provenance: "schedule_derived"` answering "what did
  the close post?" in one query.
- **Provenance is derived, not hardcoded** (#1356, migration 0035). Every entry
  that arrived over a connection claimed to be hand-entered. Provenance now
  follows the event's source, a backfill repairs the rows already written, and
  a third event class, `operational`, gives a non-economic occurrence — a
  schedule set up, a pipeline lead — an honest home.
- **A fulfilled event can be retracted while its rows are still drafts**
  (#1311): an asset disposal could only be posted and then reversed. The
  retraction is guarded so it never orphans an effect the books already hold.
- The demos abort on a dropped write instead of closing periods over a gap
  (#1318, #1320), and stop double-booking schedule periods (#1316).

## Platform and data plane

- `change-tier` refuses the sale unless the target tier has a healthy writer
  with a free slot — the rule checkout already applies — and the migration's
  drain refuses rather than timing out into a detach (#1305).
- An immediate `delete-graph` suspends the graph inline instead of advertising
  it as active until the next sensor tick (#1317). The orphan-registration
  sweep exempts deleted rows, ending a page that fired for a week after every
  deletion (#1367).
- A failed Dagster run of any job pages: the Dagster stack finally receives
  `SNSAlertEmail`, so its alarms exist, and a `RunFailure` metric has one
  (#1297).
- `getAvailableExtensions` returns the display name it was computing and
  dropping (#1321).
- The Graph API requires its cluster key on every route except `/health`
  (#1314). The HNSW branch of its vector search route is gone — HNSW indexes
  are searched in Cypher — and the call sites that read `QueryResult` rows
  through a guard that was always false share one reader (#1368, #1369).

## Security and hygiene

- Redirect URI validation on the MCP OAuth server is hardened (#1282).
- Counterparty tax identifiers reach the analytical graph as their last four
  characters, and email verification, reset and invitation tokens travel by
  reference rather than in Dagster run config (#1284).
- The WAF's request-body SQL-injection match no longer applies to the SQL
  query surface, which carries user SQL by contract and keeps its own controls
  (#1298).
- The OIDC deploy roles trust GitHub's immutable subject beside the classic
  one, which a renamed repository needs (#1371); the frontend repositories'
  OIDC variables are set from this repo's bootstrap (#1347).
- The runtime image drops `curl` and `git`, and health probes are a stdlib
  script (#1340). uv is pinned in one place, and two majors are held with the
  reason recorded in-tree (#1332, #1334).

## Infrastructure and CI

- Nothing reaches a registry for a production run that was never approved: the
  image build sits behind the deployment gate, and the gate runs first so
  approval is immediate while the tests run (#1283, #1286).
- Every pull request is classified, and a code change waits for the automated
  review before its check passes (#1341, #1342).
- Release bodies had been bare commit stats since early August because the
  generator discarded a thinking model's text block. Fixed, and the
  tag-release workflow is parameterized so the organization's other
  repositories share one copy (#1343, #1344, #1345).
- SSM tunnels bind offset local ports — `15432`, `16379`, `18000`, `18002` —
  so the local stack stays up while a tunnel is open and a command left on a
  default port can never reach production (#1350). `/hotfix` is the one
  explicit trigger for the two-PR release flow (#1300).
- `just demo` is the suite, and the demos share one operation-status reader
  (#1313, #1319).

## Deploying this release

- **Migration**: the series carries one extensions migration, `0035` (the
  `operational` event class and the `Entry.provenance` backfill, fanned out
  over every tenant schema), shipped in 1.11.15 — already applied wherever that
  patch was deployed. A fresh environment applies it at boot.
- **Stack updates** ride the deploy: `api` and `worker` take a new
  `PublicDataBucketArn` parameter with a read-only grant on the public data
  bucket, which the block tools read in-cluster; `dagster` gains the
  run-failure alarm and now receives `SNSAlertEmail`; `s3` attaches the
  `noindex` response-headers policy; `waf` carries the `BlockSqliBody` rule;
  `bootstrap-oidc` trusts the immutable subject and names the viewer
  repository. Every parameter is supplied by the workflows.
- **Owner steps**: `just bootstrap-oidc` after merge to apply the trust-policy
  change. Bedrock access to Claude Sonnet 5 must be in place in the account;
  the API task role's Marketplace permission carries the product id.
- **After the deploy, two backfills the data needs**: rebuild the SEC text
  index (`sec_ixbrl_index` with `force_reindex`) so existing documents pick up
  the complete continuation chains and the parts; then the corpus reprocess,
  which is the artifact backfill — every filing the drain processes writes its
  holon through xbrlkit 0.15.0 — followed by `sec_catalog` with
  `full_rebuild: true`. Until a filing is reprocessed the block tools answer
  404 for it.
- **Feature flags**: `CONNECTION_MERCURY_ENABLED` and
  `MERCURY_API_KEY_CONNECTIONS_ENABLED` default off (the latter is never on in
  hosted production); `SEC_FILING_ARTIFACTS_ENABLED` defaults on;
  `XBRL_KEEP_TEXTBLOCKS_INLINE` is a local control experiment only. New
  secrets: `MERCURY_CLIENT_ID`, `MERCURY_CLIENT_SECRET`, `MERCURY_ENVIRONMENT`,
  `HF_TOKEN`.
- **SDKs**: `robosystems-client` and `@robosystems/client` moved from 1.12.2
  to 1.17.0 across the series, generated from this API line: the Tavi flavor
  (1.15.0), the Mercury provider and its connection config (1.17.0),
  `classified` on the event-block transition, `journalEntries`,
  `chartTemplates`, `initialize-chart-of-accounts`, `is_active`, the operator
  endpoint's 202 contract, `queue_position` and `/resume`. The two view
  operations `disclosures` and `information-block` are additive generated-tier
  surface for the next client minor. One generated-tier removal to name:
  client 1.12.2 dropped three proof-of-concept facade methods
  (`analyze_financials`, `research`, `rag`) that nothing called (#1310).
  Nothing on the stable tier changes.
